subject: Use when designing or auditing dependency structure: package boundaries, runtime vs build dependencies, adapter…

evals.prompt: Define dependency-architecture in 2-3 sentences. Include the work it owns and the kind of user request that should activate it.
Explain why an agent would need the dependency-architecture skill instead of relying on generic reasoning. Name the failure it prevents.
Describe the mental model or main primitives behind dependency-architecture. Keep it operational rather than just naming the topic.
A user asks: "choose between Next.js, Remix, and Astro for a new app". Should dependency-architecture activate? Explain the boundary and name the better owner when possible.
evals.negative_expectation: Must not force dependency-architecture onto a request it explicitly excludes or that belongs to refactor, system-interface-contracts, version-control, framework-fit-analysis, owasp-security, architecture-decision-records, code-review.

evals.prompt: A user asks: "audit whether this repo has duplicate-purpose dependencies and unsafe package boundaries". Show the first concrete steps an agent should take when applying dependency-architecture.

Place dependency-architecture among its adjacent skills (refactor, system-interface-contracts, version-control, framework-fit-analysis, owasp-security, architecture-decision-records, code-review). What does it own, and what does it verify with or defer to?
evals.negative_expectation: Must not collapse related skills into interchangeable names; ownership must be mechanism-level.

evals.prompt: Name one plausible misconception about dependency-architecture and correct it with a mechanism-level explanation.
